_description: Phase 4 catalog: full specification for every candidate recommended as a real calculator (classification calculator or calculator-educational). Formula families and category/subcategory are cross-validated against calculator-candidates.json and calculator-formula-families.json at generation time, not hand-copied.

calculators.name: ROAS Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Revenue generated per unit of ad spend.
validationRules: output is a multiplier (2.5x), not a percentage - do not append %

calculators.name: Marketing ROI Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Net return on marketing investment as a percentage of cost.
validationRules: output is a percentage, distinct from ROAS's multiplier - do not conflate the two on the same page
edgeCases: revenue < cost -> negative ROI is valid and expected

calculators.name: Incremental ROAS Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Revenue actually caused by the ad spend (from a holdout test), divided by that spend.
validationRules: requires a true randomized holdout; a non-random control group invalidates the result
edgeCases: controlRevenue > testRevenue -> negative incremental ROAS is valid (ads suppressed organic-equivalent behavior)

calculators.name: CTR (ads) Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Share of impressions that were clicked.
validationRules: clicks should not exceed impressions in normal ad delivery
edgeCases: clicks = impressions -> 100%, flag as suspicious click fraud pattern

calculators.name: CPC Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Average price paid per click.

calculators.name: CPM Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Cost to reach 1,000 impressions.
validationRules: the x1000 factor is part of the definition - do not report raw cost-per-impression

calculators.name: CPA Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Average price paid per conversion.
validationRules: keep the conversion definition (lead vs sale vs signup) explicit next to the result - the same spend against a looser definition silently understates CPA

calculators.name: CPL Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Average price paid per lead generated.

calculators.name: CPI (cost per install) Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Average price paid per app install.

calculators.name: CPV (cost per view) Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Average price paid per (qualifying) video view.
validationRules: 'view' definition (e.g. 30s watched, or completed) must be stated - platforms differ

calculators.name: CPE (cost per engagement) Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Average price paid per tracked engagement action.
validationRules: 'engagement' has no fixed cross-platform definition (like, share, save, swipe-up all count on different platforms) - state which events are included

calculators.name: Frequency Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Average number of times a unique person was exposed to the ad.
validationRules: frequency is always >= 1 in a correct dataset; a result < 1 signals a data error, not a real value

calculators.name: Video Completion Rate Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Share of started video views that played to completion.

calculators.name: Share of Voice Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Your share of total category ad impressions in a market.
validationRules: totalMarketImpressions is rarely directly known - usually estimated from a competitive intelligence tool; state the source

calculators.name: CAC Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Total acquisition spend divided by new customers acquired.
validationRules: spend should include the full acquisition cost base being measured (paid-only vs blended) - state which

calculators.name: Blended CAC Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Total acquisition spend across every channel (including $0-cost organic) divided by all new customers, regardless of source.
validationRules: totalCustomers must include organic/referral customers, not only paid-attributed ones, or the result is really Paid CAC mislabeled

calculators.name: AOV Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Average revenue per completed order.

calculators.name: Units per Transaction Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Average number of items per completed order.

calculators.name: Revenue per Visitor Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Average revenue generated per site visitor.

calculators.name: Cart Abandonment Rate Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Share of started carts that never converted, at a chosen funnel stage.
validationRules: the stage label must be shown in the result, since cart-stage and checkout-stage numbers are not comparable to each other

calculators.name: Discount Rate Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Discount given as a share of original price.

calculators.name: Return Rate Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Share of sold units later returned.
validationRules: measured in units - do not silently substitute a revenue figure (see Refund Rate for the currency-based counterpart)

calculators.name: Refund Rate Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Refunded revenue as a share of gross revenue - the currency-based counterpart to Return Rate's unit count.
validationRules: state explicitly that this is currency-based, not unit-based, so it is never silently compared to Return Rate as if identical

calculators.name: Inventory Turnover Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: How many times inventory is sold and replaced over a period.
validationRules: cogs and inventory value must cover the same period

calculators.name: Sell-Through Rate Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Share of received inventory that has sold.
validationRules: unitsSold should not exceed unitsReceived within one stocking period

calculators.name: Shipping Cost Ratio Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Shipping cost as a share of order value.

calculators.name: Gross Margin Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Revenue remaining after the direct cost of goods sold.
validationRules: cogs only - do not fold in shipping/payment fees here, that is Contribution Margin's job
edgeCases: cogs > revenue -> negative margin is valid and should display as such, not clamp to 0

calculators.name: Contribution Margin Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Revenue remaining after cost of goods sold AND other variable costs (shipping, payment fees, etc).
validationRules: variableCosts must exclude fixed costs (rent, salaries) - those belong in Break-Even, not here
edgeCases: cogs + variableCosts > revenue -> negative margin is valid

calculators.name: Profit Margin Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Net profit as a percentage of revenue, fully loaded.
validationRules: cost here is fully loaded (all costs), unlike Gross/Contribution Margin's partial cost bases
edgeCases: cost > revenue -> negative margin is valid

calculators.name: Retention Rate Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Share of existing customers retained over a period; Churn Rate is its complement (1 - retention).
validationRules: churnRate is always reported as 1 - retentionRate, never independently re-derived
edgeCases: endCustomers - acquiredCustomers can be negative if churn exceeded start - display as a negative retention rate, don't clamp

calculators.name: Loyalty Program Participation Rate Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Share of customers enrolled in the loyalty program.

calculators.name: Reactivation Rate Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Share of lapsed customers who returned.

calculators.name: Average Customer Lifetime Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Modeled average customer lifetime (in the same period unit as the churn rate), not an observed fact.
validationRules: churnRate must be > 0 (a 0% churn model implies infinite lifetime - reject, don't return Infinity)
this is a steady-state model, not a cohort-observed number - label it as modeled

calculators.name: Logo Churn Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Customer-count churn (as opposed to revenue churn) - the SaaS-standard framing of Churn Rate.
validationRules: counts customers/accounts, not revenue - see Revenue Retention Calculator for the dollar-weighted version

calculators.name: Repeat Purchase Rate Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Share of customers who purchased more than once.

calculators.name: Delivery Rate Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Share of sent emails that were actually delivered.

calculators.name: Open Rate Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Share of delivered emails that were opened.
validationRules: Apple MPP and similar privacy features inflate opens - flag results near or above 100% as unreliable, not impossible
edgeCases: opens > delivered can legitimately occur due to proxy pre-fetching - do not clamp to 100%, but flag it

calculators.name: Click-to-Open Rate (CTOR) Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Of the people who opened, the share who clicked - isolates content/offer quality from deliverability.
validationRules: do not confuse with Email CTR (clicks/delivered) - CTOR removes deliverability/open-rate noise from the content-quality question

calculators.name: Bounce Rate (email) Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Share of sent emails that bounced.
validationRules: hard bounces and soft bounces should be labeled separately if the input distinguishes them - a blended number hides list-hygiene problems

calculators.name: Unsubscribe Rate Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Share of delivered emails that triggered an unsubscribe.

calculators.name: Complaint Rate Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Share of delivered emails marked as spam.
validationRules: rates above ~0.1% put sender reputation at risk - worth a threshold note, not a hard validation error

calculators.name: List Growth Rate Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Net change in list size over a period.
validationRules: can be negative if losses exceed gains - do not clamp

calculators.name: Revenue per Recipient Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Average revenue generated per email sent.

calculators.name: Activation Rate Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Share of installs who reached the product's defined activation event.
validationRules: the activation event is product-defined - state it next to the result, it is not a generic funnel step

calculators.name: DAU/MAU Stickiness Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: How often the average monthly user returns daily - a proxy for habit formation.

calculators.name: D1 Retention Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Share of a signup cohort that returned on day N (N is an input, not a fixed day).
validationRules: the day value must be shown in the result - D1 and D30 numbers are never comparable to each other

calculators.name: Uninstall Rate Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Share of installs later uninstalled.
validationRules: uninstalls should not exceed installs within the measured window

calculators.name: Average Session Length Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Average duration of a session.

calculators.name: Sessions per User Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Average number of sessions per active user in the period.

calculators.name: ARPDAU Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Average revenue per daily active user - a daily-window metric, not to be confused with monthly ARPU.
validationRules: revenue and dau must both be measured on the SAME day - mixing a monthly revenue figure with a single day's DAU misstates the result by ~30x

calculators.name: MRR Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Sum of all active subscription value normalized to a monthly figure; ARR = MRR x 12, growth rate compares two periods' MRR.
validationRules: annual contracts must be normalized to a monthly value before summing, not counted at face value
mrrGrowthRate is only computed when priorMrr is provided and > 0
edgeCases: priorMrr omitted or 0 -> growth rate omitted from output, not shown as 0% or Infinity

calculators.name: ARPU Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Average revenue per account; optionally divided again by avg seats per account for a true per-user figure.
validationRules: ARPU and ARPA are the same number unless avgSeatsPerAccount is supplied - only then do they diverge
edgeCases: avgSeatsPerAccount omitted -> only arpu is returned

calculators.name: Net Revenue Retention (NRR) Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Revenue retained from the existing base, with (NRR) or without (GRR) expansion revenue counted.
validationRules: GRR excludes expansion by definition (numerator caps at startingMrr) - it can equal but never exceed 100%; NRR has no such cap and can exceed 100%
edgeCases: contraction + churnedMrr > startingMrr -> both metrics can go negative, valid

calculators.name: SaaS Quick Ratio Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Growth MRR relative to lost MRR - how much you're growing for every dollar lost.
edgeCases: churnedMrr + contractionMrr = 0 -> undefined (infinite ratio), show '-' not Infinity

calculators.name: SaaS Magic Number Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Net new ARR generated per dollar of the PRIOR quarter's sales & marketing spend.
validationRules: must use the PRIOR quarter's spend, not the current quarter's - using the same quarter for both understates efficiency because current spend hasn't converted yet

calculators.name: Rule of 40 Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Combined growth-plus-profitability health check.
validationRules: both inputs are percentages already, and are ADDED as percentage points - never multiply or compound them
either input may legitimately be negative
edgeCases: both negative -> a valid (very low) score, not an error

calculators.name: Burn Multiple Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Cash burned per dollar of new ARR generated - lower is more efficient.
validationRules: netNewArr must be > 0 (undefined if ARR shrank - the ratio is not meaningful for a contracting business)
edgeCases: netNewArr = 0 or negative -> undefined, show '-' with an explanatory note rather than a misleading negative multiple

calculators.name: Annual Contract Value (ACV) Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Average annualized value of a contract.
validationRules: ACV is per-contract, distinct from ARPU which is per-account across the whole base

calculators.name: Seat Utilization Rate Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Share of purchased seats actually in active use.

calculators.name: LTV Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Simple/historic model: average order value times annual purchase frequency times customer lifespan in years. Two other legitimate models exist - see calculator-architecture.md.
validationRules: this is the simple/historic model, not margin-adjusted - it overstates LTV for low-margin businesses; the margin-adjusted model is the one to use for LTV:CAC decisions
all three inputs must cover consistent units (per-year figures)
edgeCases: any input = 0 -> LTV = 0, which is valid, not an error

calculators.name: LTV:CAC Ratio Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: How many times a customer's lifetime value exceeds the cost to acquire them.
validationRules: use the margin-adjusted LTV model here, not the simple/historic one, or the ratio overstates payback economics - flag which model fed the input

calculators.name: CAC Payback Period Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Months to recover the cost of acquiring a customer, adjusted for gross margin.
validationRules: arpu and grossMarginPct must both be > 0 (denominator is arpu * grossMarginPct)
the margin adjustment is required, not optional - omitting it (using arpu alone) is the single most common error in this calculation

calculators.name: Break-Even Point Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Units, CAC ceiling, and ROAS floor needed to cover fixed costs, from one shared margin input.
validationRules: variableCostPerUnit must be < pricePerUnit or contribution margin is zero/negative and break-even is never reached
edgeCases: variableCostPerUnit >= pricePerUnit -> undefined, no break-even exists at this price

calculators.name: Conversion Rate Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Share of opportunities (visitors, leads, etc.) that completed the target action. Universal calculator - see calculator-formula-families.json for the 16 industry-naming variants it covers.

calculators.name: Multi-Step Funnel Analysis Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Enter N ordered funnel stages; get per-step conversion, cumulative conversion, and drop-off at each stage.

acceptedRanges.stages: each count >= 0, non-increasing is expected but not enforced

validationRules: a stage count higher than the previous stage is allowed but should be visually flagged as a likely data error, not silently accepted
edgeCases: any stage count = 0 -> that step's conversion is undefined, remaining downstream steps are not computable
calculators.formulaDisplay: Stage conversion = Next stage count ÷ Previous stage count

calculators.name: Field Abandonment Rate Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Share of users who reach a specific form field and abandon there - a per-field diagnostic, distinct from whole-form completion.
validationRules: requires field-level instrumentation (e.g. focus/blur events) - state that as a prerequisite

calculators.name: Exit Rate Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Share of pageviews on a page that were the last in the session - distinct from Bounce Rate, which counts only single-page sessions.
validationRules: must not be presented next to Bounce Rate without the distinction explained - a high-traffic page can have a high exit rate and a low bounce rate simultaneously, and that is not a contradiction

calculators.name: Landing Page Bounce Rate Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Share of sessions that viewed only one page.
validationRules: session-based, not funnel-step-based - not directly comparable to Cart Abandonment Rate despite the superficially similar shape

calculators.name: Web Engagement Rate Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Engaged sessions (meeting a platform's engagement threshold) as a share of total sessions.
validationRules: the 'engaged' threshold (e.g. GA4's 10s+/conversion/2+ pageviews definition) should be stated, since it is platform-defined

calculators.name: A/B Test Significance (z-test) Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Two-proportion z-test for whether a variant's conversion rate differs significantly from control.
validationRules: frequentist method - see Bayesian Probability to Beat Control for the documented alternative method, do not present this as the only valid approach
edgeCases: conversionsA = 0 or conversionsB = 0 -> valid, z-test still computes
very small samples (<30 per arm) -> flag result as low-confidence even if p < 0.05
calculators.formulaDisplay: z-score = (Variant rate − Control rate) ÷ Standard error

calculators.name: Confidence Interval Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Confidence interval around one observed conversion rate.
validationRules: normal-approximation interval - accurate for reasonably large n and p not near 0 or 1; flag when n*p or n*(1-p) < 5
calculators.formulaDisplay: Confidence interval = Observed rate ± (z-value × Standard error)

calculators.name: Bayesian Probability to Beat Control Calculator
calculators.formula: P(variant_rate > control_rate | data), via Beta posteriors
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Bayesian alternative to the frequentist z-test: probability the variant is actually better than control.
validationRules: a flat (1,1) prior is the honest default unless the user states a real informative prior - do not silently invent one
this answers a genuinely different question from the frequentist p-value (probability of superiority, not probability of the data under a null) - never present the two numbers as interchangeable
edgeCases: extreme priors can dominate a small sample - flag low-traffic results as prior-sensitive
calculators.formulaDisplay: Probability variant beats control, estimated from Beta distributions fitted to both observed conversion rates

calculators.name: A/B/n Multi-Variant Significance Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: A/B/n significance across 3+ variants with a multiple-comparison correction.
validationRules: at least 3 variants required (2 is just the standard A/B test)
alpha must be divided by the number of comparisons (Bonferroni) - running N uncorrected z-tests inflates the false-positive rate and must not be shipped as the default
edgeCases: a variant with 0 conversions -> still computable, its rate is 0%

calculators.name: Sample Size Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Required sample size per variant, given a baseline rate, a RELATIVE minimum detectable lift, power and significance level.
validationRules: baselineRate must be strictly between 0 and 1

mde is RELATIVE (10 means 'detect a 10% relative lift') - resolved explicitly during implementation after this was flagged as an unresolved ambiguity; converted to an absolute effect internally as baselineRate x mde before use in the formula
edgeCases: mde very small relative to baseline -> sample size can become impractically large; surface the raw number rather than capping it silently
calculators.formulaDisplay: Sample size per variant = 2 × (z-values for power and significance, summed)² × Baseline rate × (1 − Baseline rate) ÷ (Baseline rate × Relative MDE)²

calculators.name: Minimum Detectable Effect (MDE) Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Given available traffic and test duration, the smallest effect size the test can reliably detect - the inverse of Sample Size.
validationRules: solves the same equation as Sample Size Calculator for a different unknown - kept as its own tool because users arrive asking 'what can I detect', not 'how many visitors do I need'
edgeCases: samplePerVariant very small -> MDE become very large (>100%), display as-is with a 'test is underpowered' flag rather than erroring
calculators.formulaDisplay: Minimum detectable effect = √(2 × (z-values for power and significance, summed)² × Baseline rate × (1 − Baseline rate) ÷ Sample size)

calculators.name: Test Duration Estimator Calculator
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Days needed to reach the required sample size at current traffic.
validationRules: round the result UP to the nearest full week - stopping mid-week reintroduces day-of-week bias even if the raw day count is reached
edgeCases: dailyTrafficPerVariant very small -> very large day counts are valid output, not an error

calculators.name: Sample Ratio Mismatch (SRM) Check Calculator
calculators.formula: chi-square goodness-of-fit test on observed vs expected traffic split
calculators.formulaPlainEnglish: Checks whether the actual traffic split between variants matches the intended split - a guardrail on the test's validity, not on its outcome.
validationRules: expectedShare values across variants must sum to 1

a low p-value here (e.g. <0.01) means the TEST ITSELF is broken (bucketing bug, bot filtering asymmetry) - it says nothing about which variant is better and must never be read as a significance result
edgeCases: a perfectly even split with small samples can still trigger a false SRM flag - note that low-traffic tests are noisier on this check too
